name: Marvel Cinematic Universe
strap: A shared world. A personal way in.
description: Understand the MCU through its people, institutions, and connected story strands. Find a starting point without watching everything.
intro: The MCU is easier to enter when you follow a question, a person, or a corner of its world. Learn what power changes on Earth, why cosmic conflicts reach it, or what heroism means in one neighbourhood.
recommendation: Start Iron Man for the shared world’s foundation, Guardians of the Galaxy for a largely independent cosmic beginning, or Daredevil season 1 for local, character-driven lore.

entries.title: Iron Man
entries.audience: I want to understand the shared world
entries.why: A personal origin explains the MCU’s central tension: power can solve a problem and create another. The wider world arrives gradually.
entries.need: Tony’s company builds weapons; he is forced to reconsider what that means.
entries.skip: Every earlier Marvel adaptation, comics histories, and a complete franchise checklist.
entries.tradeoff: This begins an Earth-focused story. It does not explain every cosmic or mystical corner immediately.
entries.next: Follow Tony’s character route or continue to The Avengers. Add other origins when their characters interest you.

entries.title: Guardians of the Galaxy
entries.audience: I want a self-contained cosmic adventure
entries.why: A new cast learns to cooperate through one clear pursuit. You can discover the galaxy alongside them.
entries.need: The characters are outsiders with competing motives, caught in a conflict over a dangerous object.
entries.skip: All the Earth origins and Avengers films before this adventure.
entries.tradeoff: Connections to the larger saga are background at first. Jumping directly to Infinity War later would reveal earlier Guardians developments.
entries.next: Continue to Guardians Vol. 2 and Vol. 3 through the group’s existing watch route.

entries.title: Daredevil season 1
entries.audience: I want people, institutions, and local stakes
entries.why: One neighbourhood gives the conflict a human scale. The law, organised crime, and vigilantism become competing answers to the same city’s problems.
entries.need: Matt works as a lawyer and secretly confronts violence in Hell’s Kitchen.
entries.skip: The Avengers saga, cosmic lore, and the other Defenders shows before season 1.
entries.tradeoff: Its darker tone and television commitment differ from a two-hour superhero film.
entries.next: Continue season 2, The Defenders, and season 3 through Matt’s route before his later appearances.

entries.title: The Avengers
entries.audience: I want to see the team dynamic quickly
entries.why: The assembly itself introduces the people and their disagreements. A short optional origin recap fills in a few personal backgrounds.
entries.need: An intelligence agency tries to build a team capable of responding to a threat beyond conventional defence.
entries.skip: Playing catch-up with every origin first.
entries.tradeoff: The characters arrive with histories. Starting here makes some relationships less personal, but the immediate mission remains understandable.
entries.next: Choose the character you enjoyed most and follow that route. Save Infinity War and Endgame for when those relationships matter.

events.title: Iron Man
events.premise: A weapons manufacturer confronts the human consequences of his work.
events.recap: Tony builds the armour, rejects his company’s old direction, and publicly identifies himself as Iron Man. Nick Fury’s approach opens the idea of a larger team.
events.why: A clear personal origin and the recommended Earth-story entrance.

events.title: Thor
events.premise: A prince’s exile connects a family’s conflict to people on Earth.
events.recap: Thor earns the right to wield Mjolnir again. Loki’s choices turn a family dispute into a wider threat.
events.why: Useful Asgard context before The Avengers.

events.title: Captain America: The First Avenger
events.premise: Steve Rogers joins a wartime experiment while HYDRA pursues a dangerous source of power.
events.recap: Steve stops Red Skull’s immediate plan, survives in ice, and awakens in a different era.
events.why: Steve’s origin; earlier in story time than the modern films.

events.title: The Avengers
events.premise: Fury brings together people who disagree about power, responsibility, and one another.
events.recap: The team stops Loki’s invasion in New York. Their cooperation makes the Avengers a public force rather than an intelligence proposal.
events.why: A workable team entry with optional origin recaps.

events.title: Captain America: The Winter Soldier
events.premise: Steve and Natasha investigate a threat that makes their own organisation difficult to trust.
events.recap: HYDRA’s infiltration brings S.H.I.E.L.D.’s structure down. Steve discovers that the Winter Soldier is Bucky, whose recovery becomes a continuing personal concern.
events.why: The clearest route into the MCU’s institutional questions.

events.title: Guardians of the Galaxy
events.era: A different corner of the same universe
events.premise: Five outsiders become involved in a pursuit across the galaxy.
events.recap: The group defeats Ronan and chooses to remain together. The orb’s connection to an Infinity Stone links their local adventure to the wider conflict.
events.why: A welcoming cosmic beginning without the Earth films.

events.title: Daredevil season 1
events.premise: A lawyer and a crime boss have competing visions for Hell’s Kitchen.
events.recap: Matt confronts Fisk’s criminal network while deciding what his own methods cost. Fisk’s defeat ends the season’s immediate crisis but does not end their relationship.
events.why: A self-contained first season and the recommended street-level entrance.

events.title: Avengers: Age of Ultron
events.premise: An attempt to prevent future threats creates an immediate one.
events.recap: Ultron’s attack devastates Sokovia. Vision joins the conflict, while Wanda’s experience changes her relationship to the Avengers.
events.why: Introduces Wanda and Vision and sets up the team’s political divide.

events.title: Captain America: Civil War
events.premise: Political oversight and a personal crisis divide the team.
events.recap: The Accords and the truth about the Stark family turn disagreement into a rupture between Steve and Tony. The team enters later threats without its earlier unity.
events.why: Important context for the divided team; not homework before every standalone film.

events.title: Thor: Ragnarok
events.premise: Thor must face a crisis that challenges what Asgard is and whom it belongs to.
events.recap: Asgard’s people escape as its physical realm is destroyed. Their journey leads directly into the opening situation of Infinity War.
events.why: An energetic Thor entry, with greater emotional weight after his earlier films.

events.title: Avengers: Infinity War
events.premise: People from Earth and space respond to Thanos’s pursuit of the Infinity Stones.
events.recap: Thanos assembles the Stones and erases half of life. The heroes’ separate efforts cannot prevent the shared catastrophe.
events.why: A convergence point; stronger after a few chosen character routes.

events.title: Avengers: Endgame
events.premise: The surviving heroes seek a way forward after the previous film’s crisis.
events.recap: Time travel enables the heroes to restore those lost. Tony’s sacrifice, Natasha’s sacrifice, and Steve’s final choice conclude central parts of their available arcs.
events.why: Follow Infinity War. It is a payoff rather than the recommended first MCU film.

events.title: WandaVision
events.premise: Wanda and Vision appear in an increasingly strange small-town setting.
events.recap: Wanda ends the Hex after confronting its cost to Westview. Vision’s altered future and Wanda’s study of the Darkhold carry different threads forward.
events.why: Optional character depth; use Wanda’s route for the earlier emotional context.

events.title: Hawkeye
events.premise: Clint’s past complicates an attempt to spend time with his family.
events.recap: Clint and Kate confront the immediate New York conflict and Yelena’s understanding of Natasha’s death. Clint’s responsibility becomes something he must explain rather than simply carry alone.
events.why: Optional smaller-scale aftermath; the character timeline supplies prior context.

events.title: Daredevil: Born Again season 1
events.premise: Matt and Fisk meet again in a changed New York.
events.why: A later continuation, with earlier Daredevil seasons and The Defenders supplying personal history. This pilot covers its starting situation.

characters.name: Tony Stark
characters.motivation: His instinct to solve danger with technology competes with the need to trust other people.
characters.relationships: Steve challenges his view of authority; Fury offers a wider purpose.

updates.text: He turns his invention into a public identity.
His attempt to automate protection helps create the next crisis.

characters.name: Steve Rogers
characters.role: A soldier with a strong moral compass
characters.motivation: He measures institutions against the people they are supposed to protect.
characters.relationships: Natasha, Bucky, Tony, and Fury test different forms of loyalty.

characters.name: Thor
characters.motivation: He learns to separate authority and worth from inherited status.
characters.relationships: His family’s conflicts and the Avengers connect his worlds.

characters.name: Bruce Banner
characters.role: A scientist living with dangerous power
characters.motivation: Control and belonging matter as much as strength.
characters.relationships: The Avengers offer cooperation without removing his fear of harm.

characters.name: Natasha Romanoff
characters.motivation: Trust and repair become alternatives to a life defined by orders.
characters.relationships: Clint, Steve, and Fury know different parts of her history.

characters.name: Clint Barton
characters.role: An operative balancing duty and home
characters.motivation: He wants to protect people without losing the life he is protecting.
characters.relationships: Natasha, his family, and later Kate Bishop make that tension personal.

characters.name: Nick Fury
characters.motivation: He prepares for threats larger than any one institution’s reach.
characters.relationships: The Avengers and S.H.I.E.L.D. embody both his strengths and compromises.

characters.name: Wanda Maximoff
characters.motivation: Personal loss and the search for belonging shape her use of power.
characters.relationships: Vision and the Avengers connect affection to responsibility.

characters.name: Vision
characters.role: A being created through several kinds of power
characters.motivation: He seeks an ethical purpose rather than merely inheriting someone else’s design.
characters.relationships: Wanda makes his questions about humanity intensely personal.

characters.name: Peter Quill
characters.motivation: A life of evasion becomes a question of whom he will stand beside.
characters.relationships: The Guardians turn temporary alliance into a chosen community.

characters.name: Rocket
characters.role: A resourceful member of the Guardians
characters.motivation: Self-protection competes with attachment to people he does not want to lose.
characters.relationships: Groot and the wider team challenge his isolation.

characters.name: Matt Murdock
characters.motivation: He wants justice while questioning which methods remain defensible.
characters.relationships: Foggy, Karen, and Fisk test his responsibilities in different ways.

characters.name: Wilson Fisk
characters.role: A powerful figure in New York
characters.motivation: His claim to improve the city conflicts with his need to control it.
characters.relationships: Matt, Vanessa, and the people beneath his influence reveal the costs.

basics: Armour, experiments, magic, and alien cultures create different kinds of power. The recurring question is who should decide how it is used.
Intelligence agencies, governments, companies, and local authorities can protect people and pursue control at the same time.
A standalone story can introduce its immediate conflict. Crossovers gain meaning from the characters you chose to follow, rather than from memorising every reference.
factions: An intelligence organisation trying to respond to unfamiliar threats. Its authority and methods are part of the story’s questions.
An authoritarian movement rooted in Steve’s wartime history. Its later role belongs inside the relevant story reveals.
Asgard’s culture and other cosmic powers have interests beyond Earth. They connect through characters and objects, not one unified alien agenda.
Powerful objects link several early conflicts. Their full consequences are revealed in the crossover recaps.
Matt, Fisk, lawyers, journalists, and neighbourhood communities ask what protecting a city actually requires.
timeline_help: These strands share one continuity; the filter separates scale and subject, not alternative universes. Story order places Steve’s origin first. The timeline is a selected lore map, not a complete franchise watch list. Use a character’s full viewing route for the films and seasons between these milestones.
scope: First lore pilot: selected origins, institutional changes, cosmic connections, and the Infinity Saga’s main convergence points, with smaller-scale aftermath. This is not a full MCU chronology or every released title. Born Again coverage is introductory. Later characters, mystic lore, and multiverse branches are reserved for later batches; the existing screen routes already provide their viewing selections.
